# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

title trainingSchool Model

class Course {
    id : String
    documents : List<Document>

    name : String
}

}

    id : String
}

    name : String
    courses : List<Course>
    sectors : List<Sector>
    addCourse(id : String) : boolean
    addSector(id : String) : Sector
    assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
}
class Sector {
    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}
class Session {
    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}
class Trainer {
    contractor : boolean
}

Course --> "*" Document : documents
Course --> Sector : sector  'opposite: courses
Course *-- "*" Session : sessions
Participant --|> Person
School *-- "*" Course : courses

Sector --> "*" Course : courses  'opposite: sector
Session --> "*" Participant : registeredParticipants
Session --> Trainer : trainer
Trainer --|> Person
@enduml

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

- The course is present in courses at most once.

- removeCourse(course : Course) : void

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary:
Adds a session to this course for the specified date, enforcing at most one session per course per day.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that date is not null and conforms to LocalDate semantics.
2. Search sessions for an existing session whose date equals the given date.
3. If such a session exists, do not create a new one; return the current sessions list.
4. Otherwise, create a new Session with the given date and no trainer/participants.
5. Append the new session to sessions.
6. Return the up-to-date sessions list.
Related Features:
- id
- sessions
- addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
- cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Session
Input:
- date: the session date in LocalDate format; logically corresponds to yyyy-MM-dd.
- The date must be a valid calendar date.
Output:
- List<Session>: the current list of sessions of this course after the operation.
- The returned list includes the newly created session if insertion succeeds.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- date is not null.
Post-condition:
- If no session existed on date, exactly one new session for that date is added.
- There is at most one session per course for any calendar day.
- The returned list reflects the current sessions state.

Course::addDocument
Summary:
Adds a referenced document to this course if it is not already associated with the course.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Check whether documents already contains a document with the same name as doc.name.
3. If a document with the same name exists, return false.
4. Otherwise, append doc to documents.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- id
- documents
- addDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
- removeDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
Related Classes: Document
Input:
- doc: Document to be added.
- doc.name is the document name and should be non-empty.
- Document names are treated as the identity within one course.
Output:
- boolean: true if the document is successfully added; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- doc is not null.
- The caller intends to add a document reference to this course.
Post-condition:
- If the result is true, documents contains doc exactly once.
- If the result is false, documents is unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary:
Cancels an existing session of this course on the specified date, but only if no participants are registered in that session.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that date is not null.
2. Find the session in sessions whose date equals the given date.
3. If no such session exists, return false.
4. If the session has any registered participants, return false.
5. Remove the session from sessions.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- id
- sessions
- addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
- cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input:
- date: the date of the session to cancel, in LocalDate format.
- The date must match an existing session date.
Output:
- boolean: true if the session is found and removed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- date is not null.
- If the targeted session has participants, it is not eligible for cancellation.
Post-condition:
- If the result is true, the session for the given date is removed from sessions.
- If the result is false, sessions remains unchanged.
- Sessions with participants are preserved.

Course::removeDocument
Summary:
Removes a referenced document from this course if present.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Search documents for a document matching doc by name.
3. If not found, return false.
4. Remove the matching document from documents.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- id
- documents
- addDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
- removeDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
Related Classes: Document
Input:
- doc: Document to be removed.
- doc.name is used as the matching key and should be non-empty.
Output:
- boolean: true if the document is removed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- doc is not null.
Post-condition:
- If the result is true, documents no longer contains the matched document.
- If the result is false, documents is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary:
Adds a session to this course for the specified date, enforcing at most one session per course per day.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that date is not null and conforms to LocalDate semantics.
2. Search sessions for an existing session whose date equals the given date.
3. If such a session exists, do not create a new one; return the current sessions list.
4. Otherwise, create a new Session with the given date and no trainer/participants.
5. Append the new session to sessions.
6. Return the up-to-date sessions list.
Related Features:
- id
- sessions
- addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
- cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Session

- The date must be a valid calendar date.
Output:

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary:
Replaces the current trainer of this session with a new trainer, only if the operation is performed strictly before the session date.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that newTrainer and today are not null.
2. If today is not strictly earlier than date, return false.
3. Set trainer to newTrainer.
4. Return true.
Related Features:
- date
- trainer
- assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
- replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
- newTrainer: trainer that will replace the current one.
- today: current date.
Output:
- boolean: true if replacement succeeds; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The session instance exists.
- newTrainer is not null.
- today is not null.
- today must be strictly earlier than date.
Post-condition:
- If true, trainer references newTrainer after the call.
- If false, trainer is unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary:
Registers a participant for this session if the participant is not already enrolled.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that p and today are not null.
2. If today is after the session date, return false only if business rules disallow late registration; however the requirement does not prohibit same-day registration, so do not reject based on date alone.
3. If registeredParticipants already contains p, return false.
4. Add p to registeredParticipants.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- date
- registeredParticipants
- registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
- trainer
Related Classes: Participant

- p: participant to be registered.
- today: current date; included for consistency with the model, but no additional restriction is required by the requirement.
Output:
- boolean: true if the participant is added; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The session instance exists.
- p is not null.
- today is not null.
- The participant is not already registered for this session.
Post-condition:
- If true, registeredParticipants contains p exactly once.
- If false, registeredParticipants is unchanged.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary:
Assigns a trainer to this session only if the assignment happens strictly before the session date.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that t and today are not null.
2. If today is not strictly earlier than date, return false.
3. If trainer is already assigned, replace it only if this operation is intended as initial assignment; otherwise use replaceTrainer.
4. Set trainer to t.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- date
- trainer
- assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
- replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Trainer

- today: current date.
- The operation is valid only when today < session date.
Output:
- boolean: true if the trainer is assigned; otherwise false.

- The session instance exists.
- t is not null.
- today is not null.
- today must be strictly earlier than date.

- If false, trainer is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

School::addSector
Summary:
Adds a new sector to the school using a unique sector ID.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that id is not null or empty.
2. Search sectors for an existing sector whose id matches id.
3. If a match exists, return null or the existing sector? 
   Since the class diagram specifies return type Sector, infer that the operation returns the created sector on success and null on failure.
4. Otherwise create a new Sector with id.
5. Add the new sector to sectors.
6. Return the new sector.
Related Features:
- name
- courses
- sectors
- addSector(id : String) : Sector
Related Classes: Sector
Input:
- id: unique sector identifier.
- id must be non-empty.
Output:
- Sector: the newly created sector when successful; null when the sector already exists or input is invalid.
Pre-condition:
- The school instance exists.
- id is not null and not empty.
- No existing sector in the school has the same id.
Post-condition:
- If successful, sectors contains a new Sector with the given id.
- If unsuccessful, sectors is unchanged.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary:
Assigns a course to a sector, ensuring the course belongs to exactly one sector at a time.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that courseId and sectorId are not null or empty.
2. Locate the course with id == courseId and the sector with id == sectorId.
3. If either is missing, return false.
4. If the course currently belongs to another sector, remove the course from that sector first.
5. Set the course's sector to the target sector.
6. Add the course to the target sector's course list if not already present.
7. Return true.
Related Features:
- courses
- sectors
- addCourse(id : String) : boolean
- addSector(id : String) : Sector
- assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input:
- courseId: unique ID of the course to assign.
- sectorId: unique ID of the sector to receive the course.
Output:
- boolean: true if assignment succeeds; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The school instance exists.
- A course with courseId exists.
- A sector with sectorId exists.
- The identifiers are not null or empty.
Post-condition:
- If true, the course is removed from any previous sector and added to the target sector.
- The course.sector reference points to the target sector.
- The course appears in exactly one sector's course list, namely the target sector.
- If false, no associations are changed.

School::addCourse

Adds a new course to the school using a case-sensitive unique course ID.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that id is not null or empty.
2. Search courses for an existing course whose id exactly matches id.

4. Otherwise create a new Course with id.
5. Add the new course to courses.
6. Return true.

- assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary:
Adds a session to the course for the specified date, ensuring at most one session per day.
Algorithm:
1. If date is null, return the current sessions list unchanged.
2. If a session already exists in sessions with the same date, do not add a new one.
3. Otherwise create a new Session with the given date and no trainer/participants yet.
4. Add the new session to sessions.
5. Return the up-to-date sessions list.
Related Features:
- sessions
- id
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input:
- date: a LocalDate value in yyyy-MM-dd format.
- date should represent the intended session day for this course.
Output:
- List<Session>: the course's current session list after the operation.
- The returned list contains no more than one session for the same date.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- date is a valid LocalDate value.
Post-condition:
- If no session existed on the given date, one new session is added.
- If a session already existed on the given date, no duplicate session is created.
- The returned list reflects the current content of sessions.

Course::removeDocument
Summary:
Removes a referenced document from this course.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Search documents for a document equal by name to doc.
3. If not found, return false.
4. Remove the matching document from documents.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- documents
Related Classes: Document
Input:
- doc: the Document object to remove.
- The document is identified by its name.
Output:
- boolean: true if the document was removed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- doc is not null.
- The course may or may not already contain the document.
Post-condition:
- If true, the matched document is no longer in documents.
- If false, documents remains unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary:
Cancels a session of this course for the specified date, but only if the session has no registered participants.
Algorithm:
1. If date is null, return false.
2. Find the session in sessions whose date equals the given date.
3. If no such session exists, return false.
4. If the session has any registeredParticipants, return false.
5. Remove the session from sessions.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- sessions
Related Classes: Session, Participant, LocalDate
Input:
- date: a LocalDate value in yyyy-MM-dd format identifying the session to cancel.
Output:
- boolean: true if the matching session was removed successfully; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- date is valid and not null.
- A session matching the given date may or may not exist.
Post-condition:
- If true, the matching session is removed from sessions.
- If false, sessions remains unchanged.
- A session with registered participants is never removed.

Course::addDocument
Summary:
Adds a referenced document to this course.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. If a document with the same name already exists in documents, return false.
3. Append doc to documents.
4. Return true.
Related Features:
- documents
- id
Related Classes: Document
Input:
- doc: a Document object to be attached to the course.
- doc.name must be a non-empty string.
- Document names are treated as identifiers within a course; duplicate names are not allowed.
Output:
- boolean: true if the document was added successfully; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- The input document is not null.
- The course does not already contain a document with the same name.
Post-condition:
- If true, doc is included in documents exactly once.
- If false, documents remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

Session::assignTrainer

4. Return true.

- date
- trainer

- If false, trainer remains unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary:

4. Return true.

- trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate

- today: the current date as LocalDate.

- The session exists.

- today and session.date are valid LocalDate values.
- today must be strictly earlier than session.date.
Post-condition:
- If true, trainer references newTrainer.
- If false, trainer remains unchanged.

2. If today is after session date, return false.

4. Add p to registeredParticipants.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- date
- registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant, LocalDate
Input:
- p: the Participant to register.
- today: the current date as LocalDate.
Output:
- boolean: true if the participant was added successfully; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The session exists.
- p is not null.
- today is not null.
- The session date is valid.
- Duplicate registration for the same participant is not allowed.
Post-condition:
- If true, p appears exactly once in registeredParticipants.
- If false, registeredParticipants remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
School::assignCourseToSector
Summary:
Assigns an existing course to an existing sector, ensuring the course belongs to exactly one sector at a time.
Algorithm:
1. If courseId or sectorId is null, return false.
2. Find the course in courses by exact id match.
3. Find the target sector in sectors by exact id match.
4. If either is missing, return false.
5. If the course already belongs to a sector, remove the course from its current sector.
6. Set the course's sector reference to the target sector.
7. Add the course to the target sector's course list if not already present.
8. Return true.
Related Features:
- courses
- sectors
Related Classes: Course, Sector

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

  public EList<Session> addSession(final LocalDate date)

  {

    }

    }
  }

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::assignCourseToSector
Summary:
Assigns a course to a sector, ensuring the course belongs to exactly one sector at a time.
Algorithm:
1. Find the course by courseId in school.courses.
2. Find the sector by sectorId in school.sectors.
3. If either is missing, return false.
4. If the course already belongs to a sector, remove the course from its current sector.courses and clear the course.sector reference.
5. Add the course to the target sector using sector.addCourse(course).
6. Set course.sector to the target sector.
7. Return true.
Related Features:
- School.courses
- School.sectors
- School.assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
- Course.sector
- Sector.courses
- Sector.addCourse(course : Course) : void
- Sector.removeCourse(course : Course) : void
Related Classes: School, Course, Sector
Input:
- courseId: the identifier of the course to assign.
- sectorId: the identifier of the destination sector.
Output:
- boolean: true if the course is successfully assigned to the sector; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The school exists.
- A course with courseId exists in school.courses.
- A sector with sectorId exists in school.sectors.
Post-condition:
- If true, the course is removed from its previous sector if any, and added to the new sector.
- The course.sector reference points to the new sector.
- The course belongs to exactly one sector after completion.
- If false, no association changes are made.

School::addCourse
Summary:
Adds a new course to the school using a case-sensitive unique course ID.
Algorithm:

2. Search school.courses for a course whose id exactly matches the given id.
3. If a match exists, return false.
4. Create a new Course with id.
5. Add the new course to courses.
6. Return true.

Pre-condition:

- The id is valid, non-null, non-empty, and not already used by another course in the school.
Post-condition:
- If true, school.courses contains a new course with the given id.
- If false, school.courses remains unchanged.

School::addSector

4. Create a new Sector with id.
5. Add it to sectors.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::removeDocument
Summary:
Removes a referenced document from the course.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Search course.documents for an equal document, using document name as identity within the course.
3. If not found, return false.
4. Remove the document from documents.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- Course.documents
- Course.removeDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
Related Classes: Document, Course
Input:
- doc: the Document instance to remove.
Output:
- boolean: true if the document is removed; false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
- The course exists.
- The provided document is not null.
Post-condition:
- If true, the document is no longer present in course.documents.
- If false, course.documents remains unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary:
Cancels an existing course session by date, but only if the session has no registered participants.
Algorithm:
1. Validate date as LocalDate.
2. Search course.sessions for a session with the given date.
3. If no such session exists, return false.
4. If the matching session has any registeredParticipants, return false.
5. Remove the session from sessions.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- Course.sessions
- Course.cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
- Session.date
- Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Session, Participant, Course
Input:
- date: the session date in LocalDate format (yyyy-MM-dd) identifying the session to cancel.
Output:
- boolean: true if the session is found and removed; false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
- The course exists.
- The date is a valid LocalDate.
- The session to be canceled, if present, must have zero registered participants.
Post-condition:
- If true, the session on the given date no longer exists in course.sessions.
- If false, course.sessions remains unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary:
Adds a referenced document to the course if it is not already associated with the course.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null or doc.name is empty, return false.
2. Check whether a document with the same name already exists in this course.documents list.
3. If such a document exists, return false.
4. Add doc to documents.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- Course.documents
- Course.addDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
Related Classes: Document, Course
Input:
- doc: a Document instance to be attached to the course.
- doc.name: the document name; must be non-empty and treated as the identity of the document within a course.
Output:
- boolean: true if the document is successfully added; false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
- The course exists.
- The provided document is not null.
- The document name is valid and unique within this course.
Post-condition:
- If the result is true, the document is present in course.documents exactly once.
- If the result is false, course.documents remains unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary:
Adds a new session to the course on the specified date, ensuring at most one session per course per day.
Algorithm:
1. Validate date format/semantic validity as LocalDate (yyyy-MM-dd).
2. If date is null or invalid, return the current sessions list unchanged.
3. Search course.sessions for a session whose date equals the given date.
4. If a session already exists for that date, do not add a new one.
5. Otherwise create a new Session with the given date and no trainer/participants.
6. Add the new session to sessions.
7. Return the updated sessions list.
Related Features:
- Course.sessions
- Course.addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
- Session.date
- Session.trainer
- Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Session, Course, Trainer, Participant
Input:
- date: the session date in LocalDate format, representing a calendar day (yyyy-MM-dd).
Output:
- List<Session>: the updated list of sessions for the course, ordered as maintained by the course.
Pre-condition:
- The course exists.
- The date is a valid LocalDate.
- The course does not already have a session on the given date to add a new one; if it does, no duplicate is created.
Post-condition:
- If the date was not already present, a new session with that date is added to course.sessions.
- The returned list reflects the current state of course.sessions.
- No more than one session exists for the course on the same date.

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary:
Removes a course from the sector and clears the course's sector reference if it points to this sector.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing.
2. If course is not present in sector.courses, do nothing.
3. Remove course from sector.courses.
4. If course.sector == this sector, set course.sector to null.
Related Features:
- Sector.courses
- Sector.removeCourse(course : Course) : void
- Course.sector
Related Classes: Sector, Course
Input:
- course: the Course to remove from the sector.
Output:
- void
Pre-condition:
- The sector exists.
- The course is not null.
Post-condition:
- If the course was associated with this sector, it is no longer in sector.courses.
- The course.sector is cleared when it referenced this sector.

Sector::addCourse
Summary:
Adds a course to the sector and synchronizes the course's sector reference.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing or reject; in this model, treat as no-op.
2. If the course already belongs to this sector, ensure it is present in courses and return.
3. If the course belongs to another sector, remove it from that sector first.
4. Add course to this sector.courses if not already present.
5. Set course.sector to this sector.
Related Features:
- Sector.courses
- Sector.addCourse(course : Course) : void
- Course.sector
Related Classes: Sector, Course
Input:
- course: the Course to be added to the sector.
Output:
- void
Pre-condition:
- The sector exists.
- The course is not null.
Post-condition:
- The course is contained in sector.courses.
- The course.sector reference equals this sector.
- A course is associated with at most one sector.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary:
Removes a course from the sector and clears the course's sector reference if it points to this sector.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing.
2. If course is not present in sector.courses, do nothing.
3. Remove course from sector.courses.
4. If course.sector == this sector, set course.sector to null.
Related Features:
- Sector.courses
- Sector.removeCourse(course : Course) : void
- Course.sector
Related Classes: Sector, Course
Input:
- course: the Course to remove from the sector.
Output:
- void
Pre-condition:
- The sector exists.
- The course is not null.
Post-condition:
- If the course was associated with this sector, it is no longer in sector.courses.
- The course.sector is cleared when it referenced this sector.

Sector::addCourse
Summary:
Adds a course to the sector and synchronizes the course's sector reference.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing or reject; in this model, treat as no-op.
2. If the course already belongs to this sector, ensure it is present in courses and return.
3. If the course belongs to another sector, remove it from that sector first.
4. Add course to this sector.courses if not already present.
5. Set course.sector to this sector.
Related Features:
- Sector.courses
- Sector.addCourse(course : Course) : void
- Course.sector
Related Classes: Sector, Course
Input:
- course: the Course to be added to the sector.
Output:
- void
Pre-condition:
- The sector exists.
- The course is not null.
Post-condition:
- The course is contained in sector.courses.
- The course.sector reference equals this sector.
- A course is associated with at most one sector.

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary:
Assigns a trainer to the session only if the operation is performed strictly before the session date.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that today and the session date are valid LocalDate values.
2. If t is null, return false.
3. If today is not strictly earlier than session.date, return false.
4. If session.trainer is already assigned, replace it with t only if this operation is allowed as assignment; otherwise use replaceTrainer for replacement semantics.
5. Set session.trainer = t.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- Session.date
- Session.trainer
- Session.assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Session, Trainer
Input:
- t: the trainer to assign.
- today: the current date used to enforce the before-session rule.
Output:
- boolean: true if the trainer is assigned successfully; false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
- The session exists.
- t is not null.
- today is a valid LocalDate.
- today must be strictly earlier than session.date.
Post-condition:
- If true, session.trainer references t after execution.
- If false, session.trainer remains unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary:
Replaces the current trainer with a new trainer only if executed strictly before the session date.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that newTrainer and today are valid.
2. If newTrainer is null, return false.
3. If today is not strictly earlier than session.date, return false.
4. Replace session.trainer with newTrainer.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- Session.trainer
- Session.replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
- Session.date
Related Classes: Session, Trainer
Input:
- newTrainer: the trainer that will replace the existing trainer.
- today: the current date, which must be strictly earlier than the session date.
Output:
- boolean: true if replacement succeeds; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- The session exists.
- newTrainer is not null.
- today is a valid LocalDate.
- today must be strictly earlier than session.date.
Post-condition:
- If true, session.trainer references newTrainer after execution.
- If false, session.trainer remains unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary:
Registers a participant for a session if the participant is not already enrolled.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that today is a valid LocalDate and p is not null.
2. Check whether p already exists in registeredParticipants.
3. If already registered, return false.
4. Add p to registeredParticipants.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- Session.registeredParticipants
- Session.registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
- Session.date
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input:
- p: the participant to register.
- today: the current date. It is accepted as an input parameter by the model even if no additional date constraint is specified for registration.
Output:
- boolean: true if the participant is added; false if already registered or input is invalid.
Pre-condition:
- The session exists.
- p is not null.
- today is a valid LocalDate.
- The participant is not already in registeredParticipants.
Post-condition:
- If true, p is contained in registeredParticipants exactly once.
- If false, registeredParticipants remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

class Course {

    removeCourse(course : Course) : void

    contractor : boolean
}

# Operation Specifications
Course::cancelSession
Summary:
Cancels a session on the given date only if that session has no registered participants.
Algorithm:
1. If date is null, return false.
2. Find the session in sessions whose date equals date.
3. If no such session exists, return false.
4. If the session has any registeredParticipants, return false.
5. Remove the session from sessions.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- sessions
- cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Session
Input:
- date: target session date in LocalDate / yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output:
- Returns true if the session is found and removed.
- Returns false if the date is invalid, the session does not exist, or the session already has participants.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- date is a valid LocalDate value.
Post-condition:
- If true is returned, exactly one session with the given date is removed from sessions.
- If false is returned, sessions remains unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary:
Adds a new session on the given date to this course, ensuring at most one session per day per course.
Returns the updated list of sessions.
Algorithm:
1. If date is null, return the current sessions list unchanged.
2. If a session already exists in sessions with the same date, return the current sessions list unchanged.
3. Create a new Session with date = date, empty registeredParticipants, and no trainer.
4. Add the new session to sessions.
5. Return sessions.
Related Features:
- sessions
- addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
Related Classes: Session
Input:
- date: session date in LocalDate / yyyy-MM-dd format.
- The date must be a valid calendar date.
- A course may have zero or more sessions, but only one session per date.
Output:
- Returns the course's up-to-date sessions list.
- The returned list reflects the current sessions after insertion or no-op.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- date is a valid LocalDate value.
Post-condition:
- If the date was not already used, a new session for that date exists in sessions.
- If the date was already used, sessions is unchanged.
- The returned list is the current sessions list stored by the course.

Course::addDocument
Summary:
Adds a document to this course's referenced document list if it is not already present.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Check whether a document with the same name already exists in documents.
3. If such document exists, return false.
4. Append doc to documents.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- documents
- addDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
Related Classes: Document
Input:
- doc: the document to be added.
- The document must have a non-empty name.
- Document names are treated as identifiers within a course; duplicate names are not allowed.
Output:
- Returns true if the document is successfully added.
- Returns false if the input is invalid or a document with the same name already exists in the course.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- doc is not null and doc.name is defined.
Post-condition:
- If the result is true, documents contains doc exactly once.
- If the result is false, documents remains unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary:
Removes a referenced document from this course if it exists.
Algorithm:
1. If doc is null, return false.
2. Search documents for a document with the same name as doc.name.
3. If no such document exists, return false.
4. Remove the matching document from documents.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- documents
- removeDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
Related Classes: Document
Input:
- doc: the document to be removed.
- The document is identified by its name.
Output:
- Returns true if a matching document is removed.
- Returns false if the input is invalid or no matching document exists.
Pre-condition:
- The course instance exists.
- doc is not null and doc.name is defined.
Post-condition:
- If true is returned, the document with the same name as doc.name is removed from documents.
- If false is returned, documents remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary:
Assigns a trainer to this session only if the assignment is performed strictly before the session date.
Algorithm:
1. If t or today is null, return false.
2. If today is not strictly earlier than the session date, return false.
3. Set trainer to t.
4. Return true.
Related Features:
- date
- trainer
- assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
- t: the trainer to assign.
- today: the current date in LocalDate / yyyy-MM-dd format.
- today must be strictly earlier than session.date.
Output:
- Returns true if the trainer is assigned successfully.
- Returns false if the input is invalid or today is not strictly earlier than the session date.
Pre-condition:
- The session instance exists.
- t is not null.
- today is not null.
- today < session.date.
Post-condition:
- If true is returned, trainer is set to t.
- If false is returned, trainer remains unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary:
Replaces the current trainer of this session only if the replacement is performed strictly before the session date.
Algorithm:
1. If newTrainer or today is null, return false.
2. If today is not strictly earlier than the session date, return false.
3. Set trainer to newTrainer.
4. Return true.
Related Features:
- date
- trainer
- replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
- newTrainer: the trainer to assign as replacement.
- today: the current date in LocalDate / yyyy-MM-dd format.
- today must be strictly earlier than session.date.
Output:
- Returns true if the trainer is replaced successfully.
- Returns false if the input is invalid or today is not strictly earlier than the session date.
Pre-condition:
- The session instance exists.
- newTrainer is not null.
- today is not null.
- today < session.date.
Post-condition:
- If true is returned, trainer is set to newTrainer.
- If false is returned, trainer remains unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary:
Registers a participant for this session if the registration is performed strictly before the session date and the participant is not already registered.
Algorithm:
1. If p or today is null, return false.
2. If today is not strictly earlier than the session date, return false.
3. If registeredParticipants already contains p, return false.
4. Add p to registeredParticipants.
5. Return true.
Related Features:
- date
- registeredParticipants
- registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
Related Classes: Participant
Input:
- p: the participant to register.
- today: the current date in LocalDate / yyyy-MM-dd format.
- today must be strictly earlier than session.date.
Output:
- Returns true if the participant is successfully registered.
- Returns false if the input is invalid, today is not strictly earlier than the session date, or the participant is already registered.
Pre-condition:
- The session instance exists.
- p is not null.
- today is not null.
- today < session.date.
Post-condition:
- If true is returned, registeredParticipants contains p exactly once.
- If false is returned, registeredParticipants remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Sector::addCourse
Summary:
Adds a course to this sector's course list and establishes the bidirectional association.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing.
2. If course already belongs to this sector, do nothing.
3. If course belongs to another sector, remove it from that sector first.
4. Add course to this sector's courses list if not already present.
5. Set course.sector to this sector.
Related Features:
- id
- courses
- addCourse(course : Course) : void
Related Classes: Course
Input:
- course: the course to be associated with this sector.
Output:
- No explicit return value.
Pre-condition:
- This sector instance exists.
- course is not null.
Post-condition:
- The course belongs to this sector.
- This sector's courses contains the course exactly once.
- The course.sector reference points to this sector.

Sector::removeCourse
Summary:
Removes a course from this sector's course list and clears the course-to-sector association if it points to this sector.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing.
2. Remove course from courses if present.
3. If course.sector equals this sector, set course.sector to null.
Related Features:
- id
- courses
- removeCourse(course : Course) : void
Related Classes: Course
Input:
- course: the course to be removed from this sector.
Output:
- No explicit return value.
Pre-condition:
- This sector instance exists.
- course is not null.
Post-condition:
- The course is no longer present in this sector's courses list.
- If the course previously referenced this sector, its sector reference becomes null.

Sector::addCourse
Summary:
Adds a course to this sector's course list and establishes the bidirectional association.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing.
2. If course already belongs to this sector, do nothing.
3. If course belongs to another sector, remove it from that sector first.
4. Add course to this sector's courses list if not already present.
5. Set course.sector to this sector.
Related Features:
- id
- courses
- addCourse(course : Course) : void
Related Classes: Course
Input:
- course: the course to be associated with this sector.
Output:
- No explicit return value.
Pre-condition:
- This sector instance exists.
- course is not null.
Post-condition:
- The course belongs to this sector.
- This sector's courses contains the course exactly once.
- The course.sector reference points to this sector.

Sector::removeCourse
Summary:
Removes a course from this sector's course list and clears the course-to-sector association if it points to this sector.
Algorithm:
1. If course is null, do nothing.
2. Remove course from courses if present.
3. If course.sector equals this sector, set course.sector to null.
Related Features:
- id
- courses
- removeCourse(course : Course) : void
Related Classes: Course
Input:
- course: the course to be removed from this sector.
Output:
- No explicit return value.
Pre-condition:
- This sector instance exists.
- course is not null.
Post-condition:
- The course is no longer present in this sector's courses list.
- If the course previously referenced this sector, its sector reference becomes null.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::assignCourseToSector
Summary:
Assigns a course to a sector. A course may belong to exactly one sector at a time; if it already belongs to another sector, it is removed from that sector first.
Algorithm:
1. If courseId or sectorId is null, return false.
2. Find the course in courses whose id equals courseId.
3. Find the sector in sectors whose id equals sectorId.
4. If either the course or sector does not exist, return false.
5. If the course currently belongs to a different sector, remove the course from that sector.
6. If the course is already in the target sector, return true.
7. Set the course's sector to the target sector and add the course to the target sector's courses if not already present.
8. Return true.
Related Features:
- courses
- sectors
- assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input:
- courseId: identifier of the course to assign.
- sectorId: identifier of the sector to receive the course.
- Both identifiers are case-sensitive Strings.
Output:
- Returns true if the course is successfully assigned to the sector.
- Returns false if either identifier is invalid or the corresponding course/sector does not exist.
Pre-condition:
- The school instance exists.
- courseId and sectorId are not null.
- A Course with courseId exists in courses.
- A Sector with sectorId exists in sectors.
Post-condition:
- If true is returned, the course belongs to the specified sector and to no other sector.
- If the course had belonged to another sector, it has been removed from that sector's courses.
- If false is returned, the state of courses and sectors remains unchanged.

School::addSector
Summary:
Adds a new sector to the school using a unique sector ID.
Algorithm:
1. If id is null or empty, return null.
2. Search sectors for an existing sector whose id equals id.
3. If such sector exists, return that existing sector or null if duplicate creation is disallowed.
4. Create a new Sector with id = id and an empty courses list.
5. Add the new sector to sectors.
6. Return the new Sector.
Related Features:
- sectors
- addSector(id : String) : Sector
Related Classes: Sector
Input:
- id: unique sector identifier.
- The identifier must be non-empty and unique within the school.
Output:
- Returns the newly created Sector on success.
- Returns null if the id is invalid or a sector with the same id already exists.
Pre-condition:
- The school instance exists.
- id is defined and not empty.
Post-condition:
- If a sector is created, sectors contains it exactly once.
- If no sector is created, sectors remains unchanged.

School::addCourse
Summary:
Adds a new course to the school using a case-sensitive unique course ID.
Algorithm:
1. If id is null or empty, return false.
2. Search courses for a course whose id equals the given id.
3. If such a course already exists, return false.
4. Create a new Course with id = id, empty documents, no sector, and empty sessions.
5. Add the new course to courses.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- courses
- addCourse(id : String) : boolean
Related Classes: Course
Input:
- id: the unique course identifier, case-sensitive.
- id must be a non-empty String.
Output:
- Returns true if the course is successfully added.
- Returns false if the input is invalid or a course with the same id already exists.
Pre-condition:
- The school instance exists.
- id is not null and not empty.
Post-condition:
- If true is returned, courses contains exactly one new Course with the given id.
- If false is returned, courses remains unchanged.

   * 5. If the course currently belongs to a different sector, remove the course from that sector.
   * 6. If the course is already in the target sector, return true.
   * 7. Set the course's sector to the target sector and add the course to the target sector's courses if not already present.
   * 8. Return true.

   * - courses
   * - sectors
   * - assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
   * Related Classes: Course, Sector
